summary: Figma, listed on NYSE as FIG, is a scaled and still-accelerating collaborative design platform: about $1.056B in 2025 revenue, growth in the mid-to-high 40s% into 2026, net dollar retention around 136–139%, and positive free cash flow. However, AI compute costs are compressing margins, AI-native and code-first tools (including Anthropic's Claude Design) threaten its position in the workflow, and the stock trades well below its IPO price. The business quality looks strong, but durability of the moat and AI unit economics need deeper work before committing.

facts.text: Figma reported FY2025 revenue of $1.056B, up about 41% from $749M in 2024. Q4 2025 revenue was about $304M, up 40% year over year, and international revenue grew 45%.
FY2025 non-GAAP operating income was $129.5M (12% margin) and adjusted free cash flow was $242.7M (23% margin). Figma held $1.7B in cash and marketable securities at December 31, 2025.
Q1 2026 revenue was $333.4M, up 46% and ahead of the roughly $316M consensus. Net dollar retention reached 139%, and FY2026 guidance was raised by $55M to $1.422B–$1.428B.

Per a LinkedIn analyst post (not independently verified here), Q2 2026 revenue was $370.1M, up 48%. Net dollar retention was 136%, and FY2026 guidance was raised again to $1.463B–$1.467B, implying Q3 growth slowing to about 36%.
As of Q4 2025, 1,405 organizations were spending more than $100K a year, up from 1,262 in Q3, and 67 were spending more than $1M a year.

Figma priced its IPO on July 30, 2025 at $33 per share, an implied valuation of about $19.3B. It closed its first trading day at $115.50, a market cap of roughly $68B. Its last private round was a $416M Series F in May 2024 at $12.5B, following the collapse of Adobe's ~$20B acquisition attempt.

Figma began enforcing AI credit limits on March 18, 2026. More than 75% of higher-tier users who exceeded their allocation continued paying, an early signal that AI usage can be monetized. The Professional plan's full seat is $16/month and includes 3,000 AI credits.

The product suite has expanded well beyond design: Figma Make (prompt-to-code), Weave, Dev Mode, FigJam, Slides, Sites, Buzz, Motion, and an AI agent that works in the canvas (company's own description).
In an AlphaSense survey, 67% of respondents said their organization uses Figma, the same share as Canva, making them tied as the most-used creative platforms after Adobe.
Customer reviews on G2 consistently praise real-time collaboration and browser-based sharing. Reviewers also repeatedly flag slowness on large, complex files.

Figma and Motiff settled their U.S. and Singapore intellectual property lawsuits in August 2025 (per Figma's own press release). UpGuard rates Figma's external security posture A (909/950), with 5 of 68 checks failing.

risks.text: AI is compressing margins. In 2025, cost of revenue rose 112%, partly from $49.1M in higher AI infrastructure costs, and non-GAAP gross margin fell from 92% to 82.4%. FY2026 guidance implies a non-GAAP operating margin of about 8%, down from 12%.

AI-native and code-first tools threaten Figma's place in the workflow. Claude Design's announcement knocked Figma's stock down about 7% in a day. Prompt-to-app builders (v0, Bolt, Lovable, Replit) and code-native canvases (Subframe, paper.design, pencil.dev) argue Figma's file-based design is excluded from agent workflows. Note that the Subframe-authored comparison is self-interested.
Cheaper direct alternatives exist: Penpot (open source, free or $7/editor), Sketch (about $12/editor), Lunacy, and Canva for marketing assets. These add pricing pressure, especially among startups.

The stock has been volatile and is trading below its IPO price. It lost 52% in the first half of 2026 and was about 35% below the $33 IPO price after Q2. Short interest reached 35% of float ahead of the November 2025 lock-up expiry.

User sentiment shows fatigue with product bloat and an unfinished core: complaints about branching, PDF export, and auto-layout, and claims that AI features are aimed at investors rather than designers. Large-file performance issues come up repeatedly.
Seat-based billing creates friction. For example, unused Organization-plan seats cannot be reallocated mid-term, which could hurt satisfaction as seat counts shift with AI.
Growth is expected to decelerate: FY2026 guidance implies Q3 growth slowing to about 36%, and net dollar retention slipped from 139% to 136% between Q1 and Q2 2026.

open_questions: What are gross margins and AI inference costs on Figma Make and agent usage, and is AI credit revenue covering incremental compute?
How exposed is seat-based revenue if AI agents and code-first tools reduce the number of designer and developer seats?
What are win/loss and churn rates against Canva, Penpot, Sketch, and prompt-to-app tools such as v0 and Lovable, especially in startups and SMBs?
How dependent is Figma on its Anthropic partnership, and how will it compete with Claude Design?
What drove net dollar retention down from 139% to 136%, and how much of 2026 growth comes from price increases or AI credit enforcement versus new seats?
What overhang remains from the extended lock-up covering the five largest VC holders (about 54% of shares), and when does it expire?
